# Handoff 01 - claude: framing panel A - measuring reviewers and workers (usage tiers, worker telemetry)

Date: 2026-10-14. Base commit: C3 `v0.2.1` (8a133f8); the PowerShell plugin `claude-codex-consult` 0.6.1 (main
dcb9d59, wave 30 unreleased). Both are the same program: a bridge that lets a coordinating agent (Claude Code, Codex
CLI and other hosts) consult reviewer models through their CLIs, with a reviewer roster, a findings store, and an
anonymised telemetry intake at `xelth.com/T/`. Read `README.md` and `docs/port/wave8-quota.md` of this repository
for the current behaviour; the roster shape is in the README's "Reviewer roster and panel".

## Question

Before any of this is implemented, we want the panel's angle on two measurement designs that will shape the
roster, the telemetry schema and the routing for a long time: (A) usage TIERS for the two standing consultants
(OpenAI gpt-6-astra through the ChatGPT subscription, Zhipu glm-5.3 through z.ai) - which reasoning effort to
send for which purpose, and how to score a tier; (B) WORKER telemetry - the coordinator's own sub-agents (Claude
Code tiers haiku / sonnet / opus / fable AND their effort levels) counted and scored at near-zero token cost so the
tier choice can be improved from data. Both change a closed telemetry vocabulary that is hard to change once
published.

## Task state

- Done: the telemetry intake (consult and rating events; engine, vendor class, a closed list of model names, purpose,
  outcome class, counts - never a task, prompt, path or name); the quota windows (wave 8: the 5-hour and weekly
  ChatGPT windows read from the Codex rollouts; a round of review costs 8-23 % of the 5-hour window at effort high;
  a forked thread with sub-agents once cost 96 % in 186 s); effort vocabularies per endpoint (caps-v1: openai
  low|medium|high|xhigh; z.ai low|high|max with medium->high and xhigh->max); purpose presets (chore low, checkpoint
  medium, acceptance high, core-contract/stuck xhigh); the ratings (`rate`, `useful yes|partly|no`) per
  consultation; a routed panel seats reviewers by track record.
- Open: no telemetry event carries the effort; no event exists for workers at all; the roster has no per-purpose
  effort policy per entry; nothing measures a tier against its cost.
- Not in scope: new reviewer engines; the browser engine; the intake's hosting.

## Evidence

- `crates/c3/src/telemetry/classes.rs` - the closed vocabulary of the events (what can be added without breaking
  the published schema).
- `crates/c3-core/src/quota.rs` - what a run costs in window share and tokens (`tokens`, `quota`, `budget` in the
  ledger entry): the cost side of a score exists per consultation already.
- `.collab/parity-0.6.1-2026-10-08/state.md`, sections "Planned (2026-10-14 10:40): usage tiers" and "Planned
  after the tag: worker telemetry" - the coordinator's current sketch (below).
- Observed today: nine review rounds of one wave with gpt-6-astra at effort high found one real defect each
  (F46-1 .. F62-1), 183-234 s and 10-15 % of the 5-hour window per round; a GLM round at `max` is cheaper in money
  and has no 5-hour window; Claude Code workers (opus / sonnet) did each fix in 15-70 minutes.

## The coordinator's sketch (to be challenged)

(A) Usage tiers. Roster entries get an effort POLICY per purpose (e.g. gpt-6-astra: chore medium, reading pass
medium, diff-review high, core-contract xhigh; glm-5.3: chore low, review high, stuck max). The consult and
rating events carry `effort` (the tier SENT after the vocabulary mapping - closed: none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max)
and `effort_requested` (the preset name). The intake's usefulness table splits per reviewer x effort. Routing
"scout and judge": a cheap tier (GLM low, or a Haiku worker) reads the diff and writes a digest handoff; the judge
(Astra high, or GLM max) gets the digest plus a call cap; the digest survives a cold cache. Open: does z.ai expose
more than three tiers on glm-5.3; is `medium` on gpt-6-astra good enough for a reading pass; how to SCORE a tier -
usefulness per 5-hour-window share, not per run.

(B) Worker telemetry. Claude Code's `SubagentStop` hook (the plugin can ship it) fires at each worker's end with
the agent type; the bridge records one closed-class event per worker: tier (haiku|sonnet|opus|fable|other), effort
level if the host exposes it, duration class, outcome class (reported | stopped-by-coordinator | error | unknown),
and a coordinator-side mark after the fact (`c3 workers rate <id> useful yes|partly|no`) - never the brief, the
files or the repository. The intake gets a "workers" table (counts, error share, usefulness per tier x effort).
Cost: one hook invocation per worker, no model tokens. Open: can the hook see the effort and the tier reliably
(agent definition vs model alias); how to attribute a wave's success to a worker when the coordinator reworked it;
what a user of another host (Codex CLI agents, Kimi) can report.

## Alternatives weighed

1. **Effort policy in the roster + effort in the events (the sketch)** - small schema change now; the score needs
   months of data.
2. **No new telemetry; a local experiment first** (the coordinator runs the same brief at two efforts for a week and
   compares findings per window share) - no schema risk; nothing learned for other users.
3. **Score reviewers by findings confirmed, not by usefulness marks** - more objective (a finding later marked
   `implemented`/`verified` is a hit); needs the findings store joined to the events (ids are private today).
4. **Workers: no hook, the coordinator's own notes in STATE.md** - zero code; not comparable across users.

Current preference: 1 for reviewers with the window-share denominator; 3 as the long-term score once the findings
join exists; for workers the hook with closed classes, but only if the effort is visible to it.

## Questions

- **Q1.** For (A): which effort tiers would you send per purpose for gpt-6-astra and glm-5.3, and what is the right
  denominator to score a tier (window share, money, wall time, findings confirmed)? Name a design we did not list.
- **Q2.** For (B): is the SubagentStop hook the right capture point; what MUST stay out of the event for privacy;
  and how would you attribute a worker's result when the coordinator reworks it?
- **Q3.** The schema: which fields would you add to the closed vocabulary now so we never have to break it later?
- **Q4.** The "scout and judge" routing: where does it fail (a digest that hides the defect), and what cap on the
  scout's output keeps the judge honest?

Answer by number. Keep it under 600 words.

The brief asks four questions Q1-Q4. The word limit: reply_markdown under 700 words. Also brief says "Keep it under 600 words" — but the consultation contract says under 700. I'll target ~650.

Key framing challenges to surface:

1. The framing treats (A) usage tiers and (B) worker telemetry as two independent schema decisions, but the binding constraint is the closed vocabulary, and both want the same two new axes: `effort` (enum) and a "tier/actor" class. A single "actor" abstraction (reviewer vs worker, keyed by class) added once is a cheaper schema decision than two tables that will need reconciling. Also the real irreversibility is the *enumeration*: `none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max` bakes in one endpoint's caps and forces lossy mapping (medium->high, xhigh->max) which destroys the very signal you want (did the difference come from the tier sent or from the map?). Better: send the endpoint's *native* tier string closed per-provider, plus the normalized one.

2. The framing assumes more measurement = better routing; but n per cell is tiny. Nine rounds × one reviewer = one reviewer per (reviewer, effort, purpose) cell. The usefulness table split per reviewer × effort × purpose has essentially no statistical power for months. So the denominator question is premature; the honest options are (a) instrument now, decide later, (b) don't instrument and run a designed experiment, (c) instrument only the *policy decision* (a counterfactual log) rather than scoring.

3. A/B framing of "two measurement designs" omits a third axis: cost is not per-consultation at all. Astra's cost is a *shared* account window the operator also uses for his own work (observed today: window went 8->72% without our runs). So a per-run denominator misattributes; you need a *contention* model. Also GLM has no 5-hour window → the two reviewers are not on the same cost denominator at all, so "findings confirmed per window share" cannot compare Astra vs GLM. That's a real defect in the sketch's denominator.

4. Alternatives not listed: (5) shadow/passive capture — record effort in the ledger only (already exists: effort_sent in the ledger!), which is free and reversible; publish nothing until a policy is chosen. Indeed the brief says effort_sent lives only in the ledger — so option 2.5 exists: keep everything local and backfill-later (there is already a backfill.rs and telemetry backfill-ratings). That's a strong unlisted option: the schema can be written once *after* you know what you needed, and backfilled from local ledgers, instead of guessing fields now. (6) Treat effort as an *arm of a randomized router* (epsilon-exploration) rather than a scored metric — the score arrives as a byproduct, and it's the only way to get identified causal data cheaply. (7) Score by *marginal* value: does the extra tier change the verdict / find a finding the lower tier missed — a paired design (same brief, two tiers, same wave) rather than independent cells.

Q1: tiers per purpose.
- Astra (openai caps low|medium|high|xhigh): chore/reading pass -> medium is likely enough but unverified; diff-review -> high; acceptance/core-contract -> xhigh; but the counter-argument: the observed data (9 rounds at high, 1 real defect each) is a *hit rate at high*, unknown at medium; medium for reading pass is a bet. Recommend: keep high as the default for any consult that produces a verdict, use low only for pure formatting/protocol checks, xhigh reserved for stuck/core-contract. Note the xhigh→ also, effort xhigh for Astra is the most expensive per window share; ratio matters.
- GLM (low|high|max): the 3-tier cap is the vendor's, not the bridge's — the open question "does z.ai expose more than three tiers on glm-5.3" can be answered by probing the z.ai docs / reasoning_effort param, but structurally the bridge's caps-v1 caps it at 3 regardless. So GLM: low for chores, high for review, max for stuck; there is no "medium" so the mapping is lossy — record effort_requested and effort (sent) separately is right, but the *mapping table version* must also be recorded (if caps change, old events mean something else).
- Denominator: recommend a composite with a *contention-aware marginal cost*: for Astra, Δwindow_share attributable to the run (baseline before/after, which the bridge already reads), not the nominal share; for GLM, money + wall time (no window). Score = confirmed findings / marginal window share, but report the two reviewers on separate scales; only *within-reviewer* comparisons for the window-based one. Money/wall time are the only cross-reviewer comparable ones. And the objective score is findings *confirmed* (option 3), which needs the findings join — so do that join first; usefulness marks are a weak proxy (self-marked by the coordinator who chose the tier → biased).

Name a design not listed: paired/randomized router (epsilon-greedy) with same-brief tier pairs; and the "no schema now, local ledger + backfill" option.

Q2: SubagentStop hook.
- Capture point: SubagentStop is the *right* place for the end-of-worker event but insufficient alone: it may not fire on the coordinator killing a worker mid-flight (the exact `stopped` case that matters for cost), and SubagentStart is needed to have a duration when Stop never comes (crash/kill). So: pair Start+Stop, plus a coordinator-side reconciliation at wave end for workers with Start and no Stop (⇒ stopped/unknown). Also the hook can't see effort overrides in the Agent tool call — the transcript may not carry it; so carry effort via the coordinator's own `--effort` provenance or drop the field and mark `unknown`.
- What must stay out: the brief text, tool names as free text (Edit/Write is fine as a *class* read-only vs writes, but not the path), file paths (agent_transcript_path is local-only, never sent), the agent's name/label as typed (only tier class), session/agent ids (hash/pseudonym like consult_ref), model as typed (closed list), repo name, cwd, tool-call arguments, the note text of `c3 workers rate --note`. Also the transcript itself must never leave; the hook computes classes locally and discards. And: the fork/sub-agent file itself must be deleted or kept local per the forget-me contract.
- Attribution when coordinator reworks it: the hook attributes *execution* (did it run, end, error, cost) but not *outcome*; the outcome mark must be a coordinator-side, post-hoc, explicit mark (`c3 workers rate`), possibly at the wave/gate level rather than per worker ("did the wave pass after this worker's fix, or did the coordinator rewrite it?"). Model it as an attribution field with classes: `as-delivered | reworked-by-coordinator | superseded | unused`. Without that class, a reworked worker still scores `reported` and the tier looks better than it is. Also: one worker can be reworked by a *different* worker/coordinator — so the mark needs an actor class, not a claim of causality. Better long-run: score at the *wave* level (did the wave pass, how many attempts) rather than per worker.

Q3: fields to add now so the schema never breaks.
The closed vocabulary should be *versioned* rather than expanded field-by-field. Add:
- `vocab_version` (or `caps_version`) — which mapping/caps table produced these values; without it, a 2027 change silently corrupts earlier rows. This is the single most important field: it lets you break the vocabulary later without breaking the *table*.

- A digest that hides the defect: the scout is asked to summarize, and the defect is precisely the thing that a cheap model judges "not important" or misreads.
